title: I'd Like...
description: Make a polite simple request for food or a drink.
objectives: Make a polite simple request for food or a drink.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to make a polite simple request for food or a drink. The central language is would like as a fixed polite request. It belongs to the practical context of food & café english. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: would like as a fixed polite request

blocks.english: I'd like a cup of tea, please.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the i'd like... exchange.
This i'd like... model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the i'd like... exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I'd like a cup of tea, please.” and “Could I have some water?” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: would like as a fixed polite request.
